plants.title: Cantor's theorem
plants.blurb: There is no way to list all subsets of a set using the set's own elements: for any map `f` from a type `α` to its subsets, some subset is missed. (The subset `{a | a ∉ f a}` cannot be `f a` for any `a`.)

decls.name: ProofGarden.cantor
decls.doc: No function from a type to its powerset (`α → Prop`) is surjective: there is always a subset `s` that `f` never hits.
decls.statement: theorem cantor {α : Type} (f : α → (α → Prop)) : ¬ ∀ s : α → Prop, ∃ a, f a = s
decls.code:
theorem cantor {α : Type} (f : α → (α → Prop)) :
    ¬ ∀ s : α → Prop, ∃ a, f a = s := by
  intro h
  -- the diagonal set `{x | ¬ f x x}`
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := h (fun x => ¬ f x x)
  -- `ha : f a = fun x => ¬ f x x`, so evaluating at `a` gives `f a a = ¬ f a a`
  have h1 : f a a = ¬ f a a := congrFun ha a
  rcases Classical.em (f a a) with hp | hp
  · have hn : ¬ f a a := by
      rw [h1] at hp
      exact hp
    exact hn hp
  · have hp2 : f a a := by
      rw [h1]
      exact hp
    exact hp hp2

-- ProofGarden/Cantor.lean
/-!
# Cantor's theorem

There is no way to list all subsets of a set using the set's own elements:
for any map `f` from a type `α` to its subsets, some subset is missed.
(The subset `{a | a ∉ f a}` cannot be `f a` for any `a`.)
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- No function from a type to its powerset (`α → Prop`) is surjective:
there is always a subset `s` that `f` never hits. -/
theorem cantor {α : Type} (f : α → (α → Prop)) :
    ¬ ∀ s : α → Prop, ∃ a, f a = s := by
  intro h
  -- the diagonal set `{x | ¬ f x x}`
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := h (fun x => ¬ f x x)
  -- `ha : f a = fun x => ¬ f x x`, so evaluating at `a` gives `f a a = ¬ f a a`
  have h1 : f a a = ¬ f a a := congrFun ha a
  rcases Classical.em (f a a) with hp | hp
  · have hn : ¬ f a a := by
      rw [h1] at hp
      exact hp
    exact hn hp
  · have hp2 : f a a := by
      rw [h1]
      exact hp
    exact hp hp2

end ProofGarden

plants.title: Euclid's lemma
plants.blurb: If a prime divides a product, it divides one of the factors. This is the fact that makes prime factorisations unique.

decls.name: ProofGarden.euclids_lemma
decls.doc: If `p` is prime and `p ∣ a * b`, then `p ∣ a` or `p ∣ b`.
decls.statement: theorem euclids_lemma {p a b : Nat} (hp : IsPrime p) (h : p ∣ a * b) : p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b
decls.code:
theorem euclids_lemma {p a b : Nat} (hp : IsPrime p) (h : p ∣ a * b) :
    p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b := by
  by_cases hpa : p ∣ a
  · exact Or.inl hpa
  · refine Or.inr ?_
    -- `gcd p a` divides `p`, so it is `1` or `p`; it cannot be `p` since `p ∤ a`.
    have hcop : Nat.Coprime p a := by
      rcases hp.2 (Nat.gcd p a) (Nat.gcd_dvd_left p a) with h1 | h1
      · exact h1
      · exfalso
        apply hpa
        rw [← h1]
        exact Nat.gcd_dvd_right p a
    exact Nat.Coprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left hcop h

-- ProofGarden/Defs.lean
/-!
# Shared definitions

Core Lean 4 has no `Nat.Prime`, `Finset.sum` or `Nat.factorial` (those live in
Mathlib, which this garden does not use), so the few notions the theorems need
are defined here. These are definitions, not proofs: nothing here is `sorry`.
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- `IsPrime p`: `p` is at least 2 and its only divisors are 1 and `p` itself. -/
def IsPrime (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ p ∧ ∀ d, d ∣ p → d = 1 ∨ d = p

/-- `sumRange n f = f 0 + f 1 + ... + f (n - 1)` (the empty sum is 0). -/
def sumRange : Nat → (Nat → Nat) → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | n + 1, f => sumRange n f + f n

/-- The factorial `n! = 1 * 2 * ... * n`, with `0! = 1`. -/
def fact : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 1
  | n + 1 => (n + 1) * fact n

/-- The Fibonacci numbers `0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...`. -/
def fib : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 1
  | n + 2 => fib n + fib (n + 1)

end ProofGarden

-- ProofGarden/EuclidsLemma.lean
/-!
# Euclid's lemma

If a prime divides a product, it divides one of the factors. This is the fact
that makes prime factorisations unique.
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- If `p` is prime and `p ∣ a * b`, then `p ∣ a` or `p ∣ b`. -/
theorem euclids_lemma {p a b : Nat} (hp : IsPrime p) (h : p ∣ a * b) :
    p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b := by
  by_cases hpa : p ∣ a
  · exact Or.inl hpa
  · refine Or.inr ?_
    -- `gcd p a` divides `p`, so it is `1` or `p`; it cannot be `p` since `p ∤ a`.
    have hcop : Nat.Coprime p a := by
      rcases hp.2 (Nat.gcd p a) (Nat.gcd_dvd_left p a) with h1 | h1
      · exact h1
      · exfalso
        apply hpa
        rw [← h1]
        exact Nat.gcd_dvd_right p a
    exact Nat.Coprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left hcop h

end ProofGarden

plants.title: Neighbouring Fibonacci numbers are coprime
plants.blurb: Two consecutive Fibonacci numbers never share a factor bigger than 1. Running Euclid's algorithm on them just walks the sequence back down to `fib 1 = 1`.

decls.name: ProofGarden.fib_coprime_succ
decls.code:
theorem fib_coprime_succ (n : Nat) : Nat.gcd (fib n) (fib (n + 1)) = 1 := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [fib]
  | succ k ih =>
    have h : fib (k + 2) = fib k + fib (k + 1) := rfl
    show Nat.gcd (fib (k + 1)) (fib (k + 2)) = 1
    rw [h, Nat.gcd_add_self_right, Nat.gcd_comm]
    exact ih

plants.blurb: The numbers from 1 to `n` add up to `n(n+1)/2`, the trick young Gauss is said to have used to add 1 to 100 in seconds.

    omega

plants.title: Euclid: there are infinitely many primes
plants.blurb: However large a number `n` you pick, there is a prime bigger than it. (Any prime factor of `n! + 1` works: it cannot be ≤ `n`, since those all divide `n!`.)

decls.name: ProofGarden.infinitely_many_primes
decls.doc: For every `n` there is a prime `p` with `n < p`.
decls.statement: theorem infinitely_many_primes (n : Nat) : ∃ p, n < p ∧ IsPrime p
decls.code:
theorem infinitely_many_primes (n : Nat) : ∃ p, n < p ∧ IsPrime p := by
  have h2 : 2 ≤ fact n + 1 := by
    have := fact_pos n
    omega
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpd⟩ := exists_prime_factor h2
  refine ⟨p, ?_, hp⟩
  refine Classical.byContradiction fun hlt => ?_
  have hpn : p ≤ n := by omega
  have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
  have hdiv : p ∣ fact n := dvd_fact (by omega) hpn
  have h1 : p ∣ 1 := (Nat.dvd_add_right hdiv).mp hpd
  have := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) h1
  omega

-- ProofGarden/Lemmas/Factorial.lean
/-!
# Lemma: facts about the factorial

Two small facts Euclid's proof needs: `n!` is never zero, and every number
from 1 to `n` divides `n!`.
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- The factorial of any number is positive. -/
theorem fact_pos (n : Nat) : 0 < fact n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Nat.one_pos
  | succ k ih => exact Nat.mul_pos (Nat.succ_pos k) ih

/-- Every `k` with `1 ≤ k ≤ n` divides `n!`. -/
theorem dvd_fact {k n : Nat} (h₁ : 1 ≤ k) (h₂ : k ≤ n) : k ∣ fact n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => omega
  | succ m ih =>
    show k ∣ (m + 1) * fact m
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge k (m + 1) with hlt | hge
    · exact Nat.dvd_trans (ih (by omega)) (Nat.dvd_mul_left (fact m) (m + 1))
    · have hkm : k = m + 1 := by omega
      rw [hkm]
      exact Nat.dvd_mul_right (m + 1) (fact m)

end ProofGarden

-- ProofGarden/Lemmas/PrimeFactor.lean
/-!
# Lemma: every number ≥ 2 has a prime factor

The smallest divisor of `n` that is at least 2 is prime.
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- Every natural number `n ≥ 2` is divisible by some prime. -/
theorem exists_prime_factor {n : Nat} (h : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n := by
  -- Strong induction, done as ordinary induction on a bound `m ≥ n`.
  have key : ∀ m n, n ≤ m → 2 ≤ n → ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro n hn h2; omega
    | succ m ih =>
      intro n hn h2
      by_cases hp : IsPrime n
      · exact ⟨n, hp, Nat.dvd_refl n⟩
      · have hex : ∃ d, d ∣ n ∧ d ≠ 1 ∧ d ≠ n := by
          refine Classical.byContradiction fun hc => ?_
          apply hp
          refine ⟨h2, fun d hd => ?_⟩
          by_cases h1 : d = 1
          · exact Or.inl h1
          · refine Or.inr (Classical.byContradiction fun hne => hc ⟨d, hd, h1, hne⟩)
        obtain ⟨d, hd, h1, hne⟩ := hex
        have hd0 : d ≠ 0 := by
          rintro rfl
          have := Nat.eq_zero_of_zero_dvd hd
          omega
        have hle : d ≤ n := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hd
        have hd2 : 2 ≤ d := by omega
        obtain ⟨p, hp', hpd⟩ := ih d (by omega) hd2
        exact ⟨p, hp', Nat.dvd_trans hpd hd⟩
  exact key n n (Nat.le_refl n) h

end ProofGarden

-- ProofGarden/InfinitudeOfPrimes.lean
/-!
# Euclid: there are infinitely many primes

However large a number `n` you pick, there is a prime bigger than it.
(Any prime factor of `n! + 1` works: it cannot be ≤ `n`, since those all divide `n!`.)
-/

namespace ProofGarden

/-- For every `n` there is a prime `p` with `n < p`. -/
theorem infinitely_many_primes (n : Nat) : ∃ p, n < p ∧ IsPrime p := by
  have h2 : 2 ≤ fact n + 1 := by
    have := fact_pos n
    omega
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpd⟩ := exists_prime_factor h2
  refine ⟨p, ?_, hp⟩
  refine Classical.byContradiction fun hlt => ?_
  have hpn : p ≤ n := by omega
  have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
  have hdiv : p ∣ fact n := dvd_fact (by omega) hpn
  have h1 : p ∣ 1 := (Nat.dvd_add_right hdiv).mp hpd
  have := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) h1
  omega

end ProofGarden

plants.title: Nicomachus's theorem
plants.blurb: The sum of the first cubes is the square of the sum of the first numbers: `1³ + 2³ + ... + n³ = (1 + 2 + ... + n)²`.

decls.name: ProofGarden.nicomachus_step
decls.doc: Algebra step: if `2 * s = k * (k + 1)` then `s² + (k+1)³ = (s + (k+1))²`.
decls.statement: theorem nicomachus_step (s k : Nat) (h : 2 * s = k * (k + 1)) : s * s + (k + 1) ^ 3 = (s + (k + 1)) * (s + (k + 1))
decls.code:
theorem nicomachus_step (s k : Nat) (h : 2 * s = k * (k + 1)) :
    s * s + (k + 1) ^ 3 = (s + (k + 1)) * (s + (k + 1)) := by
  have hk : 2 * s * (k + 1) = k * (k + 1) * (k + 1) := by rw [h]
  have hc : (k + 1) ^ 3 = (k + 1) * (k + 1) * (k + 1) := by rw [Nat.pow_succ, Nat.pow_two]
  rw [hc]
  grind

decls.name: ProofGarden.nicomachus
decls.statement: theorem nicomachus (n : Nat) : sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i ^ 3) = (sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i)) ^ 2
decls.code:
theorem nicomachus (n : Nat) :
    sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i ^ 3) = (sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i)) ^ 2 := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [sumRange]
  | succ k ih =>
    show sumRange (k + 1) (fun i => i ^ 3) + (k + 1) ^ 3
      = (sumRange (k + 1) (fun i => i) + (k + 1)) ^ 2
    rw [ih, Nat.pow_two, Nat.pow_two]
    exact nicomachus_step (sumRange (k + 1) (fun i => i)) k (two_mul_sum_upto k)

plants.title: Lemma: every number ≥ 2 has a prime factor
plants.blurb: The smallest divisor of `n` that is at least 2 is prime.

decls.name: ProofGarden.exists_prime_factor
decls.doc: Every natural number `n ≥ 2` is divisible by some prime.
decls.statement: theorem exists_prime_factor {n : Nat} (h : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n
decls.code:
theorem exists_prime_factor {n : Nat} (h : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n := by
  -- Strong induction, done as ordinary induction on a bound `m ≥ n`.
  have key : ∀ m n, n ≤ m → 2 ≤ n → ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro n hn h2; omega
    | succ m ih =>
      intro n hn h2
      by_cases hp : IsPrime n
      · exact ⟨n, hp, Nat.dvd_refl n⟩
      · have hex : ∃ d, d ∣ n ∧ d ≠ 1 ∧ d ≠ n := by
          refine Classical.byContradiction fun hc => ?_
          apply hp
          refine ⟨h2, fun d hd => ?_⟩
          by_cases h1 : d = 1
          · exact Or.inl h1
          · refine Or.inr (Classical.byContradiction fun hne => hc ⟨d, hd, h1, hne⟩)
        obtain ⟨d, hd, h1, hne⟩ := hex
        have hd0 : d ≠ 0 := by
          rintro rfl
          have := Nat.eq_zero_of_zero_dvd hd
          omega
        have hle : d ≤ n := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hd
        have hd2 : 2 ≤ d := by omega
        obtain ⟨p, hp', hpd⟩ := ih d (by omega) hd2
        exact ⟨p, hp', Nat.dvd_trans hpd hd⟩
  exact key n n (Nat.le_refl n) h
